question.problem:
Suppose that a function $f(x,y,z)$ and all of its higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ and that

$$
{f}_{zx}(x,y,z)=-\frac{2yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},\,{f}_{yz}(x,y,z)=\frac{2xz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

 

Evaluate the following expression at the point $(1,2,1):$

$$
{f}_{zyy}(x,y,z)+{f}_{xxz}(x,y,z)
$$
question.worked_solution:
As the higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. 

Hence, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zyy}(x,y,z) & ={f}_{yzy}(x,y,z) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{yz}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{2xz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{4xyz}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

In addition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xxz}(x,y,z) & ={f}_{zxx}(x,y,z) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{zx}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\frac{2yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{4xyz}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the above, we get

$$
{f}_{zyy}(x,y,z)+{f}_{xxz}(x,y,z)=-\frac{4xyz}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}+\frac{4xyz}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}=0.
$$

Finally, 

$$
{f}_{zyy}(1,2,1)+{f}_{xxz}(1,2,1)=0.
$$
